@dmeremyanin Thanks for the thorough testing, your findings align with known issues being tracked across milestones.

The autoApprovers/route approval behavior you observed is related to bugs being actively fixed in v0.29.0 (PR #3175 by kradalby and PR #3179 — both fix route approval logic in the same policy code this PR builds on).

The DNS routing gap you identified (clients not sending DNS queries to the connector node) is exactly why kradalby placed this PR in the [v0.31.0 "DNS Work" milestone](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/milestone/16). There are foundational DNS bugs (#2899, #2782, #2753) that need to be resolved first, and then the DNS-to-connector routing can be built on solid ground.

This PR intentionally covers the policy/capability layer. The DNS integration will follow as part of the v0.31.0 DNS work. I'll fix the policy reload propagation issue in the meantime.

With `0.29` adding `nodeAttrs` a bit more thoroughly, would AppConnector support now be "just" a matter of adding support for `nodeAttrs.app` (with the aforementioned DNS caveat)? Seems like that may be a cleaner solution as it can then match how Tailscale configures app connectors and would reduces the burden on Headscale to document the custom `appConnectors` policy entry.

body:
Rebased onto current main and reworked onto `nodeAttrs`. Not asking for a review pass yet, the DNS side still belongs with v0.31.

What changed since the last push:

1. App connector config rides the `app` field on `nodeAttrs` now (@Matchlighter's suggestion) instead of the custom `appConnectors` block. There is no app-connector-specific code left in the delivery path.
2. `PolicyChange{IncludeSelf: true}` is gone. A reload sends a targeted self update only to nodes whose config actually changed, which covers the reload propagation @dmeremyanin hit.
3. Added a gate on nodeAttrs `app` capability names, mirroring what grants already do through `validateCapabilityName`. The allowlist holds `tailscale.com/app-connectors` only. Say the word if you would rather have one shared allowlist, or no gate on the nodeAttrs side.
4. Docs and `features.md` state plainly that the DNS side is missing, so App Connectors is not marked as done anywhere.

All Garnix checks are green. The GitHub Actions workflows have not run on this head, looks like they need approval for a fork PR.

message:
policy: deliver app connectors via nodeAttrs app field

nodeAttrs only carried key-only capabilities through "attr". Tailscale
also delivers valued capabilities through an "app" field, which is how
app connector configuration reaches a connector node.

Add App (tailcfg.NodeCapMap) to NodeAttrGrant and stamp it in
compileNodeAttrs alongside the key-only attrs. Payloads are passed
through opaquely; the client interprets them. Multiple nodeAttrs entries
targeting the same node accumulate their values.

App connectors ride this generic path, so they follow the existing
compileNodeAttrs -> NodeCapMap -> NodesWithChangedCapMap -> SelfUpdate
propagation without any app-connector-specific code:

  "nodeAttrs": [{
    "target": ["tag:connector"],
    "app": { "tailscale.com/app-connectors": [ {...} ] }
  }]

The capability ships to every node the target selects, regardless of
"tailscale set --advertise-connector"; this matches Tailscale, where the
client gates on its local connector flag and the payload's connectors
field.

Headscale does not yet route client DNS queries for the configured
domains to the connector, so dynamic domain discovery does not happen on
its own. Prefixes listed in "routes" are advertised as soon as the
connector receives its configuration. Documented as a limitation.

Updates #1651

integration: add app connector tests

Cover the three delivery cases end to end: a tagged node selected by the
nodeAttrs target receives both configs under
tailscale.com/app-connectors, a node with a non-matching tag receives
nothing, and a wildcard target reaches a regular node.

Configs are marshalled through appctype.AppConnectorAttr so the tests
exercise the same wire shape a Tailscale-hosted control plane emits.

Updates #1651

policy: gate nodeAttrs app capability names

Grant app capability names go through validateCapabilityName, which
rejects URL-formatted names and tailscale.com names that are not
allowlisted. The nodeAttrs app field arrived without the same guard, so
a policy could ship any tailscale.com capability to a node while nothing
on the server backs it.

Add validateNodeCapabilityName with a node capability allowlist holding
tailscale.com/app-connectors. tailscaleCapAllowlist is keyed by
tailcfg.PeerCapability and describes peer caps, so node caps get their
own map rather than an entry there. Names outside the tailscale.com
domain are operator-defined and still pass through.

The reasoning is the one already written down in nodeAttrUnsupportedCaps:
delivering a capability headscale cannot act on makes a node advertise a
feature that does not work, so reject it at policy load.

Updates #1651
